export function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
export function subtract(a, b) { return a - b; }

content.text: The mission is small and well-scoped. Let me produce the plan.

arguments.summary: Decomposed the mission into a single bounded implementation contract. The repository is a minimal ES module ("type":"module") calc library with src/calc.js exporting add and subtract, and test/calc.test.js using node:test with assert/strict. The mission requires adding an exported divide(a, b) that throws a RangeError when b === 0, adding tests for the normal and zero cases, keeping existing tests green, and not touching other files. Because all edits live in two disjoint-but-cohesive files that must change together for the tests to pass, a single contract (a-1) is the right granularity. Verification is deterministic via `npm test` (runs node --test on test/*.test.js). Risk is low: no migrations, auth, concurrency, or protocol changes; it is a trivial isolated edit.

claims.claim: src/calc.js currently exports only add and subtract; there is no divide function.
test/calc.test.js imports { add, subtract } from ../src/calc.js and uses node:test with assert/strict; existing tests are for add and subtract only.
The repo is an ES module ("type":"module"); npm test runs `node --test test/*.test.js`, which will execute the updated test file.

contracts.objective: Add an exported divide(a, b) function to src/calc.js that throws a RangeError when b is 0, and add tests covering both the normal division case and the zero-divisor case in test/calc.test.js, keeping existing tests passing.
acceptance: src/calc.js exports a divide(a, b) function.
divide(a, b) returns a / b for normal, non-zero b.
divide(a, 0) throws a RangeError with a descriptive message.
test/calc.test.js contains a test for the normal division case (e.g. divide(10, 2) === 5) and a test asserting divide(x, 0) throws RangeError.
The existing add and subtract tests still pass and their imports remain intact.
constraints: Do not modify any file other than src/calc.js and test/calc.test.js.
Do not alter the existing add/subtract exports or their existing tests.
The function must be exported using the same ES module export style as the existing code.
Throw the RangeError explicitly when b === 0 (strict equality); do not rely on native division behavior.
decisions: Single contract because the source change and its tests must land together for the suite to pass.
Use npm test (node --test test/*.test.js) as the sole deterministic verification gate.
